feed.title: Windhawk Mod Updates
feed.subtitle: Updates in the official collection of Windhawk mods

entry.title: Chrome Context Menu Items 1.1.0
entry.content:
• Add {url}, {page}, {title}, {selection}, {src} and {frame} placeholders for custom commands. Values are URL-encoded inside URLs and escaped for the command line in arguments.
  • Show entries that use {url}, {selection} or {src} only when the right-clicked item provides a value.
  • Allow placeholders in the program only inside a URL, or as the whole program for http and https links, and don't run entries that pass placeholders to batch files or shells.
  • Add a per-item "Show only on pages" setting with wildcard address patterns.
  • Add a shortcut, Ctrl+Shift by default and configurable, that shows Chrome's original page menu while held (on by default).
  • Add a toggle to hide Back, Forward and Reload, and opt-in toggles for Search Google for, Copy link to highlight, Open link in new / incognito window, Open link in another profile, Picture in picture, Loop / Show controls, Emoji, Spell check / Writing direction, Password manager / Autofill and Inspect.
  • Anti-alias rounded menu item backgrounds.
  • Check the layout of Chrome's context menu data on every menu, and turn off the features that depend on it if the layout doesn't match.

entry.title: Compact Notifications 1.2
entry.content:
• Cards come straight from the notification database, so toasts that arrive in a row show together, and an app updating a shown toast updates its card.
  • Replies are typed on the card itself and sent with the app's button (or Enter).
  • Copy button for one-time codes (in the Windows language, or English via a setting).
  • Mute button (moon, on hover): mutes an app for 15 min, 1 h, 8 h, 24 h or for good (∞); a new setting unmutes the apps muted for good.
  • Do not disturb on Windows 11 is respected.
  • Cards stay while the mouse is over them; a card goes as soon as one of its buttons is pressed.
  • Animations follow the monitor's refresh rate; new optional playful style.
  • Chat text formatting (bold, italic, underline, strike, code) can be turned off.
  • Sound plays when the card shows instead of when Windows gets to the banner later; new Sound settings (when the card shows, as Windows plays it, or none) and your own .wav file.
  • Fixes: a closed card no longer comes back, the card limit keeps reminders, alarms and calls, cards go when the app takes its toast back (e.g. a call answered in the app).

entry.title: Lock Screen Live Wallpaper 1.1.0
entry.content:
• Preview window: check fit, colors and speed without locking the PC. Open it from the settings, an optional hotkey (off by default) or an optional tray icon. It can also draw the real clock, date and status icons over the video (optional, off by default).
  • Animated GIF support, alone or inside a folder.
  • Low battery saver: lower the frame rate or the render width, or freeze on a still frame.
  • Dim setting to darken the video.
  • Folder order: random, sequential or fixed.
  • Audio fade in and out.
  • Still frame duration after boot is now a setting.
  • Cached first frames older than 30 days are deleted, and only the 5 newest others are kept.
  • Faster color processing when only brightness, contrast, gamma or dim change.
  • Fixes: padded decoder frame height (for example 1088 for 1080), audio restarting together with the video on every loop, crash guard no longer counts quick unlocks as failed starts.

entry.title: Task Manager Network Speed in Bytes 1.3
entry.content:
• Fixed: the mod failed to load when Microsoft's symbol server had no PDB for the installed Task Manager build. Added a byte-pattern fallback for all seven hooks.
  • Improved: pattern matching anchors to function starts from the executable's .pdata table, requires an exact and unique match, and refuses ambiguous matches instead of hooking the wrong function.
  • Symbol-based hooking is still tried first, and every hook remains optional. No settings changed.

entry.title: Compact RDP connection bar 3.0.0
entry.content:
Compact RDP connection bar

Shrinks the top connection bar of Remote Desktop Connection (Ctrl+Alt+Home).

The bar normally spans a large fixed width: a small button group on the left, the hostname in the middle, the window buttons on the right. This mod keeps the hostname zone, keeps the button groups, and drops the empty space between them.

Works with any number of toolbars. A toolbar whose buttons are all hidden needs no width and is simply not given any, which is what happens once the pin and quality buttons are hidden.

The right toolbar carries the window buttons - minimize, restore and close. Each can be hidden separately; hide all three and the bar shrinks to the hostname alone. A single remaining toolbar keeps the side it originally sat on, so hiding the window buttons does not move the pin group to the right.

The quality indicator is a lock icon that mstsc only shows in some sessions. Ticking the setting when it is absent changes nothing, and the bar is laid out exactly as it would be without the setting.

Screenshots

Before After After2 After3 After4

Settings

  • Text area width - target width of the hostname zone, scaled for DPI. Raised automatically when the hostname needs more room.
  • Hide pin button - hides the pin (keep on top) button.
  • Hide quality button - hides the connection quality indicator.
  • Hide lock button - hides the lock icon mstsc shows next to the quality indicator. The button is only present in some sessions; when it is absent, nothing changes.
  • Hide minimize / restore / close - hide the window buttons on the right. Hiding the close button removes the only visible way to disconnect; the session can still be closed from the taskbar icon, or Ctrl+Alt+Break leaves full screen so the bar and the window controls come back.

entry.title: Chrome clear on exit with keep sites 0.4.1
entry.content:
Chrome clear on exit with keep sites

Clear Chrome's browsing data when its last window closes normally, while keeping login cookies and ordinary site storage for domains you choose. Chrome performs the deletion. The mod supplies its settings through Chrome's native policy reader.

Cleanup is off by default. Review the keep list, then turn on Enable automatic cleanup in the mod's Settings tab. The list starts empty: enabling cleanup with no exceptions signs you out of most websites. Deleted data cannot be recovered. Enter domains such as example.com; subdomains are included. Full HTTP/HTTPS URLs are accepted, with their paths and ports ignored. Use ASCII/punycode domain names.

Check your configuration

Restart Chrome after installing the mod. At chrome://policy, select Reload policies and check these three entries:

  • ClearBrowsingDataOnExitList: browsing history, download history, cached images and files, autofill, site settings, and hosted-app data, for all time.
  • DefaultCookiesSetting: 4, making ordinary site storage session-only.
  • CookiesAllowedForUrls: your keep list, preserving cookies and ordinary storage.

The keep list does not preserve history, cache, permissions, or legacy hosted-app storage. Downloaded files, bookmarks, and saved passwords are not selected for deletion. Websites can still expire their own sessions or require a new login.

Chrome already exposes the cookie/storage controls at chrome://settings/content/siteData. This mod sets those controls and their Allowed to save data on your device exceptions from one Windhawk keep list, and adds the broader exit cleanup policy which has no equivalent Chrome setting. Another clearing extension or an existing Chrome cleanup rule can still remove the data you intended to keep.

Changes and removal

After changing settings, use Reload policies to verify the result. The mod also requests a refresh when it has observed Chrome registering its policy events. Chrome processes these requests asynchronously; the mod cannot acknowledge when Chrome has finished applying them.

To stop cleanup, turn the setting off or disable the mod, then Reload policies before closing Chrome and confirm that the supplied entries have disappeared. Chrome can otherwise retain its cached policies for the remainder of that session. The next Chrome start with the mod disabled receives no policies from this mod. No administrator prompt, PowerShell helper, or policy-removal permission is needed.

The mod runs only in Chrome's browser process and does not change its real policy registry keys or profile files. It uses private temporary storage within Windhawk's mod storage while cleanup is enabled. Inactive files can remain after Chrome exits; a later enabled start attempts to remove verified leftovers when they are no longer in use. These files are never reused as configuration or needed for backup.

Scope and limitations

  • Applies to all profiles in each Chrome browser process that loads the mod. Chrome must be allowed to load Windhawk mods.
  • Intended for personal installations. Conflicting existing local Chrome policies prevent injection; they are never replaced. Chrome's normal cloud-policy precedence still applies. Check Windhawk's mod log if the entries do not appear.
  • If a policy view cannot be prepared, Chrome uses its genuine policies for that load. The mod logs the reason; check the policy page to confirm cleanup is active. If private storage could not be initialized, save the mod's settings again to retry. Once storage is ready, reloading Chrome policies retries a failed read.
  • Chrome can show Managed by your organization while these policies are active. Chrome also disables synchronization of affected data categories.
  • Normal last-window close is the supported cleanup path. Crashes, forced termination, Windows shutdown, and some restart/quit paths can prevent completion or defer selective site-data deletion until the next start.
  • Disabling the mod cannot restore browsing data Chrome has already deleted.

Back up the source and your Windhawk settings to reproduce the configuration on a fresh Windows installation. The source's defaults do not contain your saved list.

References

  • Chrome exit cleanup policy
  • Chromium Windows policy loader
  • Chromium registry policy conversion
  • Windows application hives

entry.title: Siri Plus Launchpad 1.2.0
entry.content:
New

  • Custom liquid glass theme: your color (black to start with) solid at the top, thinning out smoothly into clear glass, with a fine line of light along the bottom edge. Its own settings: color strength at the top, how far down the color goes, the glass color, and the selection color in menus.
  • The app list follows installs and removals by itself (installers and Microsoft Store apps), without turning the mod off and on.
  • Keeps working right after a Windows update: when the symbols for twinui.pcshell.dll aren't available yet, the launcher still opens with the Windows key and the Start button in a temporary way, and goes back to the normal hook the next time the mod loads with the symbols available.

Changed

  • Stronger refraction: above 60 % the liquid glass edge gets wider and deeper. The default is now 70 %.
  • Glass themes start with the Liquid glass style.
  • The background blur chosen in the settings panel is now kept for each theme, like the glass transparency.
  • The selection color in menus also works in the Custom liquid glass theme.

Fixed

  • A newly installed app only showed up after the mod was turned off and on.

entry.title: Disable Web Search in Start Menu 1.0.0
entry.content:
Disable Web Search in Start Menu

The search UI that the Start menu and the taskbar open mixes results from Bing into local results. Windows can be told to stop doing that with settings and policies, but they are read when the search UI starts, so changing them means signing out, and the registry entries stay behind afterwards.

This mod does the same thing without touching the registry. It sits in the search UI process and answers the setting reads as if web search had been turned off. Turning the mod off gives the old behavior back the next time the search UI starts.

On both Windows 10 and Windows 11, typing in the Start menu hands the query to this search UI, so the Start menu search is covered as well.

Settings

  • Also hide cloud content results reports the two "Cloud content search" switches from Settings as off. The Windows 11 search UI asks for them before it puts web results in the list, so turning this setting off can bring web results back, and leaving it on also removes OneDrive, Outlook and SharePoint results from search.

Notes

  • Nothing is written to the registry and no files are touched. The values the mod reports are the ones Windows itself uses:
    • DisableSearchBoxSuggestions, ConnectedSearchUseWeb and DisableWebSearch, the web search policies
    • BingSearchEnabled, the older web results switch
    • IsMSACloudSearchEnabled, IsAADCloudSearchEnabled and AllowCloudSearch, the cloud content switches, only with the setting above If you set any of these yourself, the mod simply agrees.
  • The search UI is a packaged app and reaches the registry through the API sets, which end up in kernelbase.dll. Desktop callers import advapi32.dll, whose exports are separate entry points rather than forwarders on current builds. Both are hooked, so neither path is missed.
  • Web results are decided while the search UI sets up, so after enabling the mod or changing a setting, end SearchHost.exe in Task Manager. Windows starts it again on the next search, and the new settings are read then.
  • If web results survive, turn on the mod's log and open the search UI once. The log lists every read the mod answered, which shows whether the process asks for these values at all.

entry.title: Dynamic Island Media Player 1.6.0
entry.content:
Dynamic Island Media Player for Windows

A focused, customizable Dynamic Island overlay for Windows that becomes an interactive media player when music or video is playing. Based on the original Dynamic Island for Windows, this standalone mod removes unrelated dashboard modules and concentrates on media playback.

Key Features

  • Media integration: Track title, artist, album, source-app badge, album artwork, playback state, and progress information through Windows System Media Transport Controls. Artwork is refreshed when metadata settles, stale provider thumbnails are rechecked briefly, and large covers are downscaled to reduce memory use.
  • Playback controls: Play/pause, previous/next track, and progress scrubbing.
  • Track transitions: Choose between crossfade (Fade) and horizontal slide animations. Track transitions work independently from the option that disables the island's hover and movement animations.
  • Interactive island: Expand on hover, click-through mode with Ctrl-to-interact, and configurable show/hide, next, previous, and play/pause hotkeys.
  • Window behavior: Always-on-top, above-games behavior, taskbar layering, fullscreen handling, and per-application saved positions.
  • Context menu: Right-click configuration with color and opacity dialogs, playback-related options, and persistent menu overrides.
  • Color customization: Theme presets, background/text colors, automatic/system/custom accent colors, and a user-managed color-morphing palette with speed controls.
  • Appearance: Multiple island shapes, adjustable size and text scale, custom font, button styles, shadow toggle, and monitor selection.
  • Localization: Ukrainian, Russian, and English interface languages.
  • Media source filtering: Optionally restrict the player to the currently selected media source.

Credits

  • Himanshu (devcode90): Original Dynamic Island for Windows framework, rendering foundation, and core interface design.
  • BOG090909: Standalone media-player adaptation, per-app positioning, customization features, localization, playback integration, and performance improvements.

entry.title: Window Wobble 1.0.1
entry.content: • Fixed the window stretching off screen and disappearing for a moment when the mouse button was released while the window was still moving. The settle animation was numerically unstable for frame times longer than 7.8 ms, so it affected 60 Hz and 120 Hz displays and any frame hitch. It is now sub-stepped and stable at any refresh rate.
